ordered.title: Signs You Need Professional Engine Fitting
ordered.description: If you already have an engine and need it fitted, professional installation is essential. Here's why you shouldn't DIY.

cards.title: ⚠️ Engine alignment
cards.text: Misaligned engine can cause vibration, premature wear, and damage to engine mounts and drivetrain components.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Engine alignment Misaligned engine can cause vibration, premature wear, and damage to engine mounts and drivetrain components.

cards.title: ⚠️ Correct torque settings
cards.text: Incorrectly torqued bolts - especially head bolts, flywheel bolts, and main bearing bolts - can cause catastrophic failure.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Correct torque settings Incorrectly torqued bolts - especially head bolts, flywheel bolts, and main bearing bolts - can cause catastrophic failure.

cards.title: ⚠️ Fluid filling
cards.text: Incorrect oil grade, overfilling or underfilling can cause immediate engine damage.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Fluid filling Incorrect oil grade, overfilling or underfilling can cause immediate engine damage.

cards.title: ⚠️ Cooling system bleeding
cards.text: Air pockets in the cooling system can cause localised overheating and head gasket failure.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Cooling system bleeding Air pockets in the cooling system can cause localised overheating and head gasket failure.

cards.title: ⚠️ Wiring and sensors
cards.text: Incorrectly connected sensors can cause engine management issues, warning lights, and drivability problems.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Wiring and sensors Incorrectly connected sensors can cause engine management issues, warning lights, and drivability problems.

cards.title: ⚠️ Exhaust connections
cards.text: Poorly fitted exhaust can cause leaks, MOT failure, and reduced performance.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Exhaust connections Poorly fitted exhaust can cause leaks, MOT failure, and reduced performance.

cards.title: ⚠️ Drivetrain alignment
cards.text: Misaligned clutch, gearbox, or propshaft can cause vibration and premature wear.
cards.fullText: ⚠️ Drivetrain alignment Misaligned clutch, gearbox, or propshaft can cause vibration and premature wear.

blocks.text: [EM-INTERVIEW] based on specialist interviews. The £800-£1,200 you save on fitting can cost you £2,000-£5,000 in engine damage.

"We see engines that were fitted by DIYers or inexperienced garages. The most common issues are incorrect torque on head bolts - leading to head gasket failure - and incorrect oil filling, which leads to bearing failure. The £800-£1,200 you save on fitting can cost you £2,000-£5,000 in engine damage."

ordered.title: Risks & Caveats of Customer-Supplied Engines
ordered.description: When you supply your own engine, you accept certain risks. Here's what you need to know.

cards.title: Risk 1: No Warranty on the Engine
cards.text: The fitter does not warrant your engine. If the engine has internal damage - even if it was supplied as "tested" - the fitter is not responsible.
cards.fullText: Risk 1: No Warranty on the Engine The fitter does not warrant your engine. If the engine has internal damage - even if it was supplied as "tested" - the fitter is not responsible. Mitigation: Have the engine inspected by a specialist before installation. Or, consider using a supply-and-fit service where the supplier warranties the engine.

cards.title: Risk 2: Compatibility Issues
cards.text: You may have sourced an engine that is not compatible with your vehicle - different engine code, different suffix, different emissions spec.
cards.fullText: Risk 2: Compatibility Issues You may have sourced an engine that is not compatible with your vehicle - different engine code, different suffix, different emissions spec. Mitigation: Verify the engine code matches exactly - including the suffix. If you're unsure, have the fitter check before installation.

cards.title: Risk 3: Missing Ancillaries
cards.text: Your engine may be missing ancillary components - turbo, injectors, alternator, starter, wiring harness.
cards.fullText: Risk 3: Missing Ancillaries Your engine may be missing ancillary components - turbo, injectors, alternator, starter, wiring harness. Mitigation: Confirm with the supplier exactly what is included. Budget for missing ancillaries.

cards.title: Risk 4: Fitment Quality
cards.text: The fitter is responsible for the installation - but if the engine fails due to internal damage, you pay.
cards.fullText: Risk 4: Fitment Quality The fitter is responsible for the installation - but if the engine fails due to internal damage, you pay. Mitigation: Choose a fitter with good reviews. Ask them to check the engine before installation.

blocks.text: "We always recommend a supply-and-fit service over customer-supplied engines. The cost difference is £300-£600 - but if the customer-supplied engine fails, they pay for removal and refitting again. That's £1,000+ extra. The supply-and-fit service gives them warranty coverage on the whole job."

ordered.title: Anecdotal Validation from UK Specialists
ordered.description: The following insights are drawn from interviews with UK engine specialists who regularly fit customer-supplied engines [EM-INTERVIEW].

blocks.text: "We see engines that have been tested and are perfect - and we see engines that are completely unusable. The problem is, without dismantling it, you can't always tell. We recommend customers have their engine inspected by a specialist before we fit it. It adds £100-£200 to the cost, but it can save £1,000+ in re-fitting costs if the engine is faulty."

"The engine arrives and it's missing the turbo or the injectors. The customer thinks they've saved £300 by buying the engine without ancillaries - but then they spend £600 sourcing them separately. And the fitting cost hasn't changed. The 'saving' disappears."

"When we fit a customer-supplied engine, we warranty our labour - typically 12 months. If the engine fails due to internal damage, we don't cover that. But if it fails because of our installation - a loose bolt, an incorrectly connected sensor - we cover it. That's your protection."

blocks.question: How much does engine fitting cost? +
blocks.answer: Engine fitting costs vary by vehicle complexity: 4-cylinder FWD £800-£1,200 , 6-cylinder RWD £1,000-£1,800 , V8 / 4WD / SUV £1,500-£2,500 , commercial / van £1,800-£3,000 .

blocks.question: What's included in the fitting cost? +
blocks.answer: Fitting typically includes: removal of the old engine, installation of your engine, basic consumables (oil, coolant, filters), basic gaskets and seals, post-installation testing, and disposal of the old engine.

blocks.question: What's NOT included? +
blocks.answer: Engine supply, warranty on the engine, collection/delivery of your vehicle, clutch/DMF, water pump/thermostat, air-con regas, ancillary parts, and unforeseen repairs discovered during fitting.

blocks.question: Do you warranty customer-supplied engines? +
blocks.answer: No - the fitter warranties their labour, not your engine. If the engine fails due to internal damage, you are responsible. This is why we recommend supply-and-fit for most customers.

blocks.question: How long does engine fitting take? +
blocks.answer: Labour typically takes 8-15 hours (1-3 days) for a standard engine, or 15-25 hours (3-5 days) for a complex installation. The average timeline from vehicle arrival to completion is 2-5 days.

blocks.question: Can I supply my own engine? +
blocks.answer: Yes - this is a labour-only service. You supply the engine, we connect you with fitters who can install it. However, we recommend having the engine inspected before installation.

blocks.question: What if my engine is faulty? +
blocks.answer: If the engine is faulty, you will need to source a replacement and pay for removal and refitting again. This is why we recommend supply-and-fit for most customers - it includes warranty coverage.

blocks.question: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? +
blocks.answer: DVLA - update the engine number on your V5C [DVLA, 2025]. Insurer - you should check with your insurer. Some policies require notification of major mechanical changes, while others may not.
